newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with WTI, flat diffs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with WTI, flat diffs.

text.p: Outright prices for U.S. West Coast light crudes fell with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Monday, while differentials held steady after two deals were struck last week.
Spot WTI prices saw little momentum besides a collapse in refined products on NYMEX, traders said.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained flat at $2.20 a barrel under Dec WTI following last week's purchases by a major West Coast refinery.
ANS outright prices were dragged down 30 cents to $21.50/21.80 a barrel on Monday.
Traders reported no new ANS deals, and saw little activity for the rest of 1996, as oil firms kept close tabs on crude inventories for tax reasons.
The operator of the trans-Alaska pipeline said Monday they would decide in the next months whether to shut two more pump stations along the 800-mile oil line.
Alyeska, the operator, said declining ANS production could prompt the next in a series of scheduled pump-station shutdowns, likely to occur next year.

The company first scheduled the shutdown of some of the pipeline's 12 pump stations last year as a response to declining production, which has fallen to 1.4 million barrels a day this year from 2.0 million in 1988.
Line 63 crude was notionally 30 cents lower, tracking WTI.
Wilmington crude remained $18.10/$18.20 a barrel, while bids for Kern River crude stayed $16.70/$16.90 a barrel.
